title: How many hours of continuing education do California real estate agents need to renew?
description: California DRE continuing education: 45 hours per renewal, mandatory topics including fair housing role play and implicit bias, and how renewals work.
shortAnswer: California real estate salespersons and brokers must complete 45 clock hours of continuing education approved by the Department of Real Estate (DRE) within the four years before each license renewal. The 45 hours must include the mandatory subjects (ethics, agency, trust fund handling, risk management, fair housing with an interactive role-play component, a two-hour implicit bias course, and, for brokers and later renewals, management and supervision) plus at least 18 hours of consumer protection courses.
keyTakeaways: Every renewal needs 45 clock hours of DRE-approved continuing education, completed within the four years immediately before the renewal takes effect.

First-time salesperson renewals need separate three-hour courses in ethics, agency, trust fund handling, risk management and fair housing, plus a two-hour implicit bias course; first-time broker renewals add management and supervision.
The fair housing course must include an interactive participatory component in which the licensee role-plays as both a consumer and a real estate professional.
For second and later renewals with expiry on or after January 1, 2023, the mandatory subjects can be covered by one nine-hour survey course or by individual courses.
At least 18 hours must be consumer protection courses. Licensees should keep certificates for four years after renewal in case the DRE asks for them.
jurisdiction: United States (California): Real Estate Law, Business and Professions Code sections 10170 onward
appliesTo: Real estate salespersons renewing for the first time or later
Real estate brokers and corporation officers
Brokerages that supervise salespersons and track their license status

sections.heading: How much continuing education does a California real estate license require?

blocks.text: Each renewal requires 45 clock hours of DRE-approved continuing education. The DRE's [continuing education requirements page](https://www.dre.ca.gov/licensees/CERequirements.html) sets the same total for salespersons, brokers and corporation officers, and varies only the mandatory subjects depending on license type and whether it is the first renewal.

The hours must fall inside a four-year window. The DRE's Continuing Education Course Verification form, [RE 251](https://www.dre.ca.gov/files/pdf/forms/re251.pdf) (Rev. 2/26), says all courses must be completed within the four-year period immediately preceding the effective date of renewal, which is normally the day after the expiration date for an on-time renewal. Course credit expires four years from the completion date, so hours used for one renewal cannot be reused for the next.

sections.heading: Which topics are mandatory in California real estate CE?

blocks.text: The mandatory subjects depend on who is renewing. The table summarizes the three cases the DRE sets out; in every case the balance of the 45 hours after the mandatory subjects must include at least 18 hours of consumer protection, and the rest may be consumer service or consumer protection.

blocks.title: Primary text: California DRE
blocks.text: "A three-hour course in fair housing, which must include an interactive participatory component during which the licensee will role-play as both a consumer and a real estate professional."

The seven mandatory subjects in the survey course are ethics, agency, trust fund handling, risk management, management and supervision, fair housing and implicit bias training. The survey course has grown over time: a DRE [advisory on Assembly Bill 345](https://www.dre.ca.gov/files/pdf/adv/AB345LicenseesAdvisory.pdf) describes an eight-hour survey course and a new broker management and supervision requirement taking effect on January 1, 2016, before implicit bias and the fair housing role play were added.

sections.heading: How do California real estate renewals and late renewals work?

blocks.text: Licensees renew through the DRE's eLicensing system or by paper application, and continuing education must be fully satisfied before an eLicensing renewal will go through. The DRE's [renewal page](https://www.dre.ca.gov/licensees/renewlicense.html) says renewal applications can be submitted 90 days before expiry, and an on-time renewal lets the licensee keep operating after the expiration date under Business and Professions Code section 10156.2 unless notified otherwise.

items: **Late renewal:** available for two years after expiry, but the person cannot perform licensed activity until renewed, and courses must fall within the four years before the DRE receives the application.
**Extension:** under section 10171.2, a qualifying licensee can request 90 extra days after expiry to submit CE evidence, using form RE 213 by mail before the license expires.
**Exemption:** under section 10170.8, a licensee aged 70 or older with 30 continuous years in good standing can request a permanent CE exemption.

blocks.text: The DRE emails a courtesy reminder about 90 days before expiry, but its renewal page is clear that not receiving the notice does not relieve the licensee of the responsibility to renew.

sections.heading: What should a California brokerage track for its licensees?

blocks.text: A brokerage should track three facts for each licensee: the license expiry date, whether the next renewal is a first renewal, and the completion dates of each mandatory course. The first-renewal flag matters because first-time renewals need separate courses rather than the survey course, and a broker's first renewal adds management and supervision.

Agents who also originate mortgage loans have a separate annual requirement; see [SAFE Act mortgage loan originator continuing education](/regulations/safe-act-mortgage-loan-originator-continuing-education).

sections.heading: How does Knowledge Foundry approach this?

blocks.text: Knowledge Foundry can sit alongside DRE-approved courses by mapping a brokerage's own policies, such as trust fund handling procedures and fair housing escalation steps, to assessable outcomes. The brokerage then holds evidence that licensees can apply its procedures, not only that they completed approved hours. See [professional services](/industries/professional-services).

faqs.q: Can California real estate CE hours be carried over to the next renewal?
faqs.a: No. RE 251 states that continuing education credit expires four years from the course completion date, so courses completed for a previous renewal cannot be applied to a current renewal application. Each renewal needs a fresh 45 hours completed within the four-year window.

faqs.q: Is implicit bias training required for every California real estate renewal?
faqs.a: Yes. First-time renewals need a separate two-hour implicit bias course, and later renewals cover implicit bias either in the nine-hour survey course or in an individual course. It is one of the seven mandatory subjects the DRE lists.

faqs.q: Do California real estate licensees send their CE certificates to the DRE?
faqs.a: Not routinely. Licensees enter course numbers and completion dates when renewing. RE 251 says certificates should be kept for four years after the renewal is complete so they can be furnished to the DRE on request.

faqs.q: What happens if a California real estate license expires?
faqs.a: The licensee cannot perform activities requiring a license until it is renewed. Late renewal is possible for two years after expiry at a higher fee, and the continuing education must have been completed within the four years before the DRE receives the late application.

factCheck.claim: 45 clock hours of DRE-approved CE; first-time salespersons: four three-hour courses (ethics, agency, trust fund handling, risk management), three-hour fair housing with interactive role play as consumer and professional, two-hour implicit bias, minimum 18 hours consumer protection.

First-time brokers or officers: five three-hour courses adding management and supervision; subsequent renewals with expiry on or after January 1, 2023: one nine-hour survey course covering seven mandatory subjects or individual courses, plus 18 hours consumer protection.

Courses must be completed within the four-year period immediately preceding the effective date of renewal; CE credit expires four years from completion; certificates kept four years after renewal; late renewals allowed two years after expiry.

CE extension of 90 days under BPC 10171.2 via RE 213 by mail before expiry; exemption under BPC 10170.8 for licensees 70 or older with 30 continuous years in good standing; on-time renewal permits continued operation under BPC 10156.2; renewal submitted 90 days before expiry; reminder email about 90 days before.

AB 345 amended BPC 10170.5 effective January 1, 2016, requiring brokers to complete a three-hour management and supervision course on first renewal and an eight-hour survey course for subsequent renewals.
